title: With Require Tech Story off, the report line ends after the description
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure Require Tech Story is off (Settings, then the Work Orders tab).
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with one labor line, line 1, titled "Replace tie rod" with the description "excessive play", approved and not yet completed.
  • Use Google Sheets (File, then Import, then Upload) to open downloaded files, so accented letters and character counts read correctly.
  • Start on work order 1, on its Lines tab.
custom_steps:
1. Complete line 1 without typing a tech story.
  2. Change work order 1's status to Complete.
  3. Click the Finance tab.
  4. Click Create Invoice.
  5. Close the New Customer Payment window without taking a payment.
  6. Click Reports in the top bar.
  7. Click Export Reports in the Reports left menu.
  8. Pick Customer Invoice in the Report Name list.
  9. Set the date range to today.
  10. Click Download.
  11. Open the downloaded file in Google Sheets.
  12. In an empty cell, enter =LEN() with line 1's ItemDescription cell inside the brackets.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Line 1 completes without asking for a tech story.

Step 2:

  • Work order 1 shows Complete.

Step 3:

  • The Finance tab opens.

Step 4:

  • A new invoice is created and work order 1 shows Invoiced.

Step 5:

  • The payment window closes.

Step 6:

  • The Reports page opens.

Step 7:

  • The Export Report dialog opens.

Step 8:

  • Customer Invoice is picked in Report Name.

Step 9:

  • The date range shows today's date.

Step 10:

  • A Customer Invoice file downloads.

Step 11:

  • In line 1's row (work order 1's new invoice) the ItemDescription cell reads exactly "Replace tie rod - excessive play".
  • There is no hyphen and no space after "excessive play", and no tech story text.

Step 12:

  • The cell shows 32 (15 + 3 + 14 = 32), so nothing is added and nothing trails after the last word.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (Title and Description), Confluence 845348896, version 15 (14 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11257, story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks)

  • S3-R6a: “A narrative is absent legitimately, not only exceptionally. The organization setting Administration, Work Order Settings, Require Tech Story governs whether the completion gate gets in the way, so a shop with it switched off invoices completed lines with no narrative as a matter of course. Shops created since the setting was introduced (June 2025) start with it off; shops that existed then started with it on. Each shop keeps the value it has set, and this change does not touch it.”
  • S3-R6: “A line with no narrative ends after the description, with no trailing hyphen and no trailing space. A narrative is absent when the value is empty, is made only of spaces, or is the literal placeholder "Tech story missing."; the three are treated identically, and none reaches QuickBooks. The Edit Line window writes the placeholder when an existing line with no tech story is saved from it; a line saved from New Line keeps an empty tech story. Neither depends on completion or on Require Tech Story.”
  • S3-R3: “A separator appears only between two segments that are both present. A line with no description joins the title straight to the narrative. A line with no narrative ends after the description. A line with neither carries the title alone. In every case there is no trailing separator and no trailing space. A segment made only of spaces counts as absent.”
  • Key Decisions: “Whether a line has a narrative at all is a shop setting, so its absence is normal rather than exceptional. Administration, Work Order Settings, Require Tech Story: "Tech story will be a required field before a line can be completed on a work order." With it on, the completion gate refuses an empty value and every invoiced line carries one. With it off, a line is completed and invoiced without one, and the text simply ends after the description.”

Not yet checked against a build by us: the QA build (sv10130.qa.shopview.com, QuickBooks host qb1.qa.shopview.com) and staging carry this change, and this case has not been run on either.

References from Design

Design canvas "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Pz1Q6BfvreYFpQwVQZPTE6), copy re-read on 27 Oct 2026 (its one change since 13 Oct: the New Line board's "Title *" now reads "Title"): board 1.3 "What reaches QuickBooks". These boards draw the line text, not a screen: the case types their example values where they fit; the expected results above come from the quotes above.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • board-1.3-what-reaches-quickbooks.png

The design's own words:

  • “Require Tech Story ON Replace tie rod - excessive play - Both outer ends worn, replaced and aligned Require Tech Story OFF, none written Replace tie rod - excessive play No trailing hyphen and no trailing space. A separator appears only when there is something on both sides of it, which is the same rule the description already follows.”
